- **The firewall is NAME-based, not capability- or dataflow-based, and the detector call site sits on the wrong side of it.** The broadcast dict `b` iterated at run.py:3417 is built at run.py:3186-3189 and carries ORACLE payload: `veh` (a full `Vehicle` with `.is_attacker`, `.is_faulty`, `.attack_type`, `.is_vru`, `.victims`, `.onset`), `x`,`y` (TRUE position), `falsified` (an oracle attack label — literally in FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_KEYS at records.py:39), `ghost`, `tspd`, `thdg` (true speed/heading). A detector writing `det["myCheck"] = 3.0 if b["falsified"] else 0.0` yields a perfect oracle in `detnorm_myCheck` and passes EVERY existing check, because the COLUMN NAME is innocuous. The only thing stopping it today is that all detector code is in-tree and reviewed — see the honour-system comments at run.py:3182-3185 ("nothing on the reception / detection path reads them") and 2632-2639.
- Therefore a third-party plugin would be subject ONLY to the name-based post-hoc lint of the final `ml/` frames (featurize.py:516), only if the user runs featurize, and only on names. It can launder any oracle value under a clean key. Two additional bypasses: (a) writing its own side-channel column via `file_report`'s `row[...]` (2623-2642) is not possible from outside, but a plugin given a mutable `det`/`row` would be; (b) a plugin that doesn't use detnorm_* at all is unlinted entirely.
- The MOSAIC side is structurally immune by construction (SignedCam.java:22-31 has no oracle handle), which is the design target: a Python plugin must receive an oracle-free frozen DTO, never `b` or `Vehicle`.

determinism_risks: Global RNG stream perturbation — the highest-severity risk. `rng.random() > cfg.report_prob` (run.py:3526) draws from the single seeded `random.Random(cfg.seed)` (run.py:1943) INSIDE the per-message reception loop. Any plugin that draws even one value from `rng` shifts every subsequent draw in the whole run and diverges the entire dataset. Mitigation already proven in-tree: per-link/per-vehicle keyed streams (run.py:3352-3353, 3563) and GeometricChannel's internal streams.

DET_KEYS ordering -> column order -> digest. `DET_KEYS` is a tuple (run.py:2570-2573) and detnorm_* keys are inserted into the report dict in that order (run.py:2641-2642); JSON serialization preserves insertion order, so the digest depends on it. A registry backed by a set, or by importlib entry_points (whose iteration order depends on installed distributions and filesystem order), would be nondeterministic across machines. The Java side already hit and fixed this exact class of bug — `LinkedHashMap` with an explicit comment at CamDetector.java:235-236 ('keeps same seed -> byte-identical robust across JDK versions').

Adding ANY unconditional detnorm_* column rewrites every ma_reports row and breaks 8 pinned golden digests: test_config_knobs.py:41,44,47; test_denm.py:50; test_combined_attacks.py:27; test_vru.py:27; test_vru_denm_harden.py:58; test_vru_spoofing.py:40 (default value 0bd93655a2d5bebb4172191fab0940a5ff90c6be685cfa033f5edcfd7c1fb740). The ONLY byte-identical path is the opt-in gating pattern at run.py:2578-2584 (`if _emit_station_type` / `if _denm_enabled`) with the enable flag defaulting off — a plugin registry MUST default to empty and MUST NOT append a column when no plugin is declared.

Plugin discovery outside the manifest breaks the replay contract. `_write_manifest` (run.py:3779-3802) serializes `cfg.__dict__` only, and `manifest_to_config` (run.py:1892-1918) is its exact inverse (test_config_io.py:33,49 assert byte-identical replay). If the detector set comes from installed packages / a plugins/ directory glob / env vars rather than from a config field, `data_digest` becomes a function of machine state and replay-from-manifest silently produces a different dataset. Java already leaks this way: CamDetector thresholds come from `System.getenv` (CamDetector.java:43-51) and are only recovered by re-publishing them into the MOSAIC manifest at ScmsBeaconApp.java:183-192.

Tie-breaking in `reasons = sorted(fired, key=lambda k: -det[k])` (run.py:3528). `fired` is built by comprehension over DET_KEYS (3523), so equal scores currently break ties by DET_KEYS position. Python's `sorted` is stable, so this is deterministic ONLY while DET_KEYS has a fixed total order — another reason the registry must be an ordered sequence, not a mapping/set.

Shared mutable per-(receiver,sender) state `st` (run.py:3422) with reserved keys 'h', 'streak', 'touch', 'kf'. A plugin writing a colliding key corrupts the built-in detectors' history/streak/tracker and silently changes the digest. Needs a namespaced sub-dict per plugin.

Float reproducibility across plugin dependencies. detnorm values are rounded only at emission (`round(det.get(k, 0.0), 3)`, run.py:2642); everything upstream is raw float64. A plugin using numpy/BLAS-backed math (or any lib with platform-varying reductions) can differ in the last ulp and cross the 1.0 firing boundary differently on another host. Compounded by the constraint that the host is Windows with no shapely/scipy and WSL disabled, so a plugin's dependency set is exactly the kind of thing that will not be identical across users. Contract should mandate pure-Python/stdlib math, or round the plugin's returned detnorm at a declared precision before the >= 1.0 comparison at run.py:3522.

Plugin-caused ordering effects in the Sybil grid: `cells` is a Counter built once per step over all broadcasts (run.py:3250-3252) and read per receiver (3450-3451). A plugin that mutates broadcasts or builds its own global aggregate must do so with the same deterministic iteration order, or per-receiver results become order-dependent.

Iteration/time/identity nondeterminism inside plugin code: `set` iteration, `dict` from unordered input, `id()`/`hash()` of objects, `time.time()`, `os.environ` reads, threading. None is currently possible in the detector path; all become possible the moment third-party code runs there. The contract should ban them explicitly and, ideally, verify with a two-run digest comparison (the pattern at test_pipeline.py:77 / test_end_to_end.py:63-64) executed over the declared plugin set.

Exception behaviour: a plugin that raises mid-run would abort before `_write_manifest`. Note the interrupt path (run.py:1924-1928) deliberately preserves a valid manifest+digest on SIGINT; a plugin error contract must be equally explicit — fail-fast before step 0 (validate at config time) rather than mid-loop, since a partially-applied plugin produces a digest that matches nothing.

Counts, for the orchestrator: Python engine = 14 hard reason codes (12 always-on, 2 opt-in-gated) + 1 soft = 15 detnorm_* columns maximum per report. MOSAIC engine = 9 hard + 1 soft = 10. The two suites are NOT interchangeable (different detector sets, different thresholds, different firing semantics: Python multi-reason, Java first-match cascade) even though featurize.py:92-103 normalizes their report rows into one table — that divergence is itself an argument for a shared plugin contract.

Answer to 'is there ANY registration mechanism': no. Zero hits for entry_points / importlib.metadata / register_detector / plugin / Protocol / abstractmethod across src/, tools/, gui/. A user must fork run.py and edit inside the `run_pipeline` closure.

Answer to 'what stops a detector from reading ORACLE ground truth': in the Python engine, nothing mechanical. run.py never calls the linter; the linter is name-based and post-hoc (featurize.py:516 on ML column names, validate.py:53 non-raising); and the detector call site has `b["veh"].is_attacker`, `b["x"]`, `b["y"]`, `b["falsified"]`, `b["tspd"]`, `b["thdg"]` in lexical scope (dict built at run.py:3186-3189). Discipline is enforced by code review and the comments at run.py:3182-3185 / 2632-2639. In the MOSAIC engine it IS structural — the detector only ever sees a SignedCam (SignedCam.java:22-31). Any plugin design must adopt the MOSAIC pattern; otherwise the leakage firewall, the project's stated core scientific-validity guarantee (leakage_linter.py:3-5), is voided the moment third-party detector code runs.

Also worth flagging to the design: `detector_outputs` (run.py:2617-2618) records only `reasons[0]`, and `detector_score_norm = max(det.values())` (2624) silently includes SOFT keys — both are shape bugs a formalized contract should fix, and both are ETSI TS 103 759 report-shape surface (manifest standards_profile at run.py:3794-3795), so they bear on the 'standards-compliant' half of the directive.
